## Claims
- [proved] Conditional on the accepted all-degree integral interval/Schur/Pieri presentation for \(p=c=1\), the missing \(k>b:=\min(i,j)\) certificate is established: \((A_+M)_{d+k}=M_{d+k}\) for every \(b<k\le i+j+1\), and \(M_{d+k}=0\) for \(k>i+j+1\).

## Strategy
Let \(d=ij\), \(A_+=(h_1,h_2,\ldots)\), and assume
\[
M=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i+1)^{j+1}}\mathbb Zs_\mu,
\]
with multiplication by \(h_t\) given by Pieri, deleting terms outside this interval.

For \(0\le k\le i+j\), put
\[
\alpha_k=\max(0,k-i),\qquad \beta_k=\min(j,k),
\]
\[
P_{x,y}=s_{((i+1)^x,i^{j-x},y)}\quad(0\le x\le j,\ 0\le y\le i),
\qquad C_x=P_{x,k-x}.
\]
Then
\[
M_{d+k}=\bigoplus_{x=\alpha_k}^{\beta_k}\mathbb ZC_x.
\]
Indeed, \(x\) is the number of the first \(j\) rows enlarged from \(i\) to \(i+1\), while \(k-x\) is the final-row length. The inequalities \(0\le k-x\le i\) and \(0\le x\le j\) are exactly
\(\alpha_k\le x\le\beta_k\).

For \(1\le t\le k\), every source in degree \(d+k-t\) is
\[
P_{u,k-t-u},\qquad \alpha_{k-t}\le u\le\beta_{k-t}.
\]
Its complete Pieri row in degree \(d+k\) is
\[
h_tP_{u,k-t-u}
=
\mathbf1_{\alpha_k\le u\le\beta_k}C_u+
\mathbf1_{\alpha_k\le u+1\le\beta_k}C_{u+1}. \tag{1}
\]
There are no further interval terms: a horizontal strip may enlarge no top row, producing \(C_u\), or one top row, producing \(C_{u+1}\); enlarging two top rows repeats column \(i+1\).

Since \(A_+=(h_1,h_2,\ldots)\),
\[
(A_+M)_{d+k}=\sum_{t=1}^{k}h_tM_{d+k-t}. \tag{2}
\]
Thus (1) is the complete positive-degree multiplication-row list.

For \(1\le k\le i+j\), the complete \(h_1\)-rows are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{condition}&\text{row}\\ \hline
k>i&h_1P_{\alpha_k-1,k-\alpha_k}=C_{\alpha_k}\\
\alpha_k\le u<\beta_k&h_1P_{u,k-1-u}=C_u+C_{u+1}\\
k>j&h_1P_{\beta_k,k-1-\beta_k}=C_{\beta_k}.
\end{array} \tag{3}
\]

Now let \(b<k\le i+j\).

If \(k>i\), retain the left singleton and all adjacent rows in (3).  In column order
\((C_{\alpha_k},\ldots,C_{\beta_k})\), their matrix is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
1&0&0&\cdots&0\\
1&1&0&\cdots&0\\
0&1&1&\ddots&\vdots\\
\vdots&\ddots&\ddots&\ddots&0\\
0&\cdots&0&1&1
\end{pmatrix},
\]
with the evident \(1\times1\) interpretation when \(\alpha_k=\beta_k\). Its determinant is \(1\).

If \(k\le i\), then \(k>b\) forces \(j=b<k\), hence \(k>j\). Retain all adjacent rows and the right singleton. Their matrix is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
1&1&0&\cdots&0\\
0&1&1&\ddots&\vdots\\
\vdots&\ddots&\ddots&\ddots&0\\
0&\cdots&0&1&1\\
0&\cdots&0&0&1
\end{pmatrix},
\]
again with determinant \(1\).

Hence the \(h_1\)-rows span \(M_{d+k}\), so by (2),
\[
(A_+M)_{d+k}=M_{d+k}\qquad(b<k\le i+j). \tag{4}
\]

At \(k=i+j+1\), the sole interval class is
\[
T=s_{(i+1)^{j+1}},\qquad M_{d+i+j+1}=\mathbb ZT.
\]
The nonzero multiplication rows are exactly
\[
h_tP_{j,i+1-t}=T\qquad(1\le t\le i+1). \tag{5}
\]
For \(u<j\), reaching \(T\) requires a box in column \(i+1\) both above and below, hence is not a horizontal strip. Thus (5) is complete and gives the unit matrix \((1)\); therefore
\[
(A_+M)_{d+i+j+1}=M_{d+i+j+1}.
\]

Finally, the interval has maximal partition \((i+1)^{j+1}\), of degree \(d+i+j+1\). Consequently
\[
M_{d+k}=0=(A_+M)_{d+k}\qquad(k>i+j+1).
\]

## Gaps
The proof is conditional on the accepted all-degree interval Schur-basis presentation and its Pieri compatibility; this certificate does not independently source-ground those hypotheses.
